name: gzip
algorithm: Inflate a gzip file of 100 MB of text with the std's decompressor, reading the output in 64 KiB chunks; the checksum adds every decompressed byte and the length; rounds times (README.md).

skip.c: no std gzip in C (zlib is not std)
skip.rust: no std gzip in Rust (flate2 is a crate; no crate stands in)
skip.mk-wrap: no checked arithmetic in the task

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; every column checks the gzip trailer's CRC-32 and length (Go's gzip.Reader inside the decompressor; the Zig program with std's flate.Container.Hasher, because Zig 0.17's Decompress reads the trailer without comparing it, BS-1; Mk's Inflater inside the decompressor, which TestGzipTrailerChecked runs too), and the checksum (the sum of the decompressed bytes plus the length) checks the output
notes: The input is wordfreq's kind of text (tools/bench gen kind words, seed 6, 100,000,000 bytes) compressed once by Go's compress/gzip at the default level (tools/bench gen kind gzip).

mk: std.compress.Inflater.NewGzip over a Reader.Of of the file's bytes (D-779), read once with fs.ReadBytes, as Go and Zig inflate from one in-memory copy; Read into a 64 KiB buffer, the window and input buffer from one arena reset after each round. The cell was held out until std had a Reader over a byte slice (review finding BF-4); it returned with M9 item 11.23 part 1, its quick_checksum shown by an untimed verify. Its trailer check is tested by TestGzipTrailerChecked.
